sources.note: Nothing. The phonological sketch on pp. 243-246 (Table 1 consonant inventory of Tanapag and southern dialects, geminates, nine vowels short and long, compensatory lengthening so that 'no noun has less than two mora in its surface free form', historical final-vowel deletion, *k loss, pronoun+aspect assimilations) never mentions stress, accent, prosody or intonation; the rest of the paper is orthography-convention history. downloaded from ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253371 (bitstream).

sources.citation: Ellis, S. James. 2012. Saipan Carolinian, one Chuukic language blended from many. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa. 440 pp.

As of this date, that kind of data has been gathered only at the periphery of other domains of linguistic inquiry.' and '(For a detailed study of prosodic elements in one of the Chuukic languages see Matsunami (1998).)' sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. & Jeffrey C. Marck (in collaboration with Jesus Mareham Elameto). 1991. Carolinian-English Dictionary. (PALI Language Texts: Micronesia.) Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press. 1229 pp. in the open PDF. DOI 10.2307/j.ctv9hvsnv
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction (pp. xv-xxiv: dialects, entry structure, long vowels and geminates written double, base forms) and 'The Sounds of Carolinian' (pp. 27-28, a letter-to-phone table with English comparisons and a note that k, p, t are unaspirated) say nothing about stress; headwords carry no stress marks (acute accent = vowel quality a/o/u). Preface p. ix: 'a planned grammatical sketch of the language was not able to be included in the Introduction'. Only lexical hits: ghoogho 'intonation, accent, speech pattern'. downloaded from ScholarSpace hdl 10125/62861.

sources.citation: Elameto, Jesus Mareham. 1977. Linguistic dimensions of vernacular education for Saipan Carolinians. MA thesis, University of Hawaii. 111 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2.2 'Carolinian Phonology and Morphology' (pp. 12-25: phonemes of the Elle dialect, consonant gemination, vowel length 'in most cases predictable', phonemic borrowing, syllable structure CV/CVC/CVVC/CCVC, reduplication, final-vowel deletion and compensatory lengthening, verb-phrase morphophonemics) has no stress or accent statement; the only 'accent' hit (p. 29) is the acute-accent vowel diacritic of the Trukese orthography. downloaded from ScholarSpace hdl 10125/76092 (open bitstream; the _uh copy is login-restricted).

sources.citation: Fritz, Georg. 1911. Die Zentralkarolinische Sprache: Grammatik, Uebungen und Woerterbuch der Mundart der westlich von Truk liegenden Atolle, insbesondere der Saipan-Karoliner. Berlin: Georg Reimer. 154 pp. (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Notation only, no rule. p. 8 'Aussprache und Lautbezeichnung' (PDF p. 24, verified on the page image): 'Soweit sie ausreichte wurde die deutsche Lautbezeichnung angewandt mit Akzenten auf den betonten Silben, Dehnungs- und Kuerzungszeichen auf den Vokalen' and 'ff, mm, nn, ll getrennt, jeder Laut fuer sich auszusprechen (wie im Italienischen). Zuweilen bildet ein solcher Konsonant eine betonte Silbe fuer sich, z. B. m in mang.' The Woerterbuch (pp. 65-154) marks an accent on nearly every entry (e.g. p. 81: toengoeg, ligaboebo, samol, faelang), so per-word stress data exist, but no placement r…

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. 1983. The internal and external relationships of the Trukic languages of Micronesia. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: The most detailed treatment of Trukic (Chuukic) phonology by the author of the Carolinian dictionary and orthography; Ellis 2012 uses it for 'most phonetic and phonological developments in the continuum'. If any Jackson work states Carolinian/Trukic stress it is this one. Not on ScholarSpace (searched); record seen in the 1991 dictionary bibliography (p. 25) and Ellis 2012 bibliography.

sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Per Ellis 2012 (p. 131) the first study that 'comes close to' a phonology of the continuum, comparing Sonsorol, Chuukese, Satawalese and Pulap; Satawalese and Puluwat/Pulap are the source dialects of southern Saipan Carolinian, so a stress statement here would transfer with an identity caveat. Record seen in Ellis 2012 bibliography.
